slides.headline: Ring Cameras Take Flight And Patrol
slides.subheadline: Two autonomous cameras bring indoor mapping, cloud processing, and physical constraints.
slides.svgBlueprint: Use the supplied palette throughout. Draw an abstract airborne camera above a curved dashed route, and a wheeled camera beside a floor-level route. Arrange the two trajectories diagonally around generous headline space. Anchor one price badge to each device. Silhouettes are conceptual, not dimensionally accurate product renderings.

slides.headline: One Shipping Schedule, One Regulatory Gate
slides.subheadline: Rover preorders are open; the drone's target still requires authorization.

items.title: Ring Rover Cam
items.body: Preorders open; shipping scheduled for December 16, 2026.

items.title: Ring Drone Cam
items.body: Target: January 27, 2027, contingent on Federal Communications Commission authorization.

slides.svgBlueprint: Create a horizontal, explicitly schematic timeline with two release nodes. Use a solid node for Rover's scheduled shipping and an outlined node behind a gate for the drone's contingent target. Place each date inside its corresponding text zone, not duplicated on an axis. Avoid a completion checkmark or any suggestion of granted authorization.

slides.headline: Autonomous Does Not Mean Local Only
slides.subheadline: Both devices combine onboard inputs with cloud processing for navigation.

items.title: Cameras And Sensors
items.body: AI Pilot uses cameras and on-device sensors.

items.title: Vision Models
items.body: Specialized vision models support autonomous route planning and obstacle avoidance.

items.title: Cloud Processing
items.body: Amazon explicitly includes cloud processing; operation is not local-only.

slides.svgBlueprint: Arrange three labeled nodes as a spacious triangle around an AI Pilot label. Represent cameras and sensors with an aperture, vision models with a layered mesh, and cloud processing with an outlined cloud. Connect nodes using neutral, undirected lines: the dossier does not establish processing order or model location. Do not depict video-upload contents.

slides.headline: Both Map Interiors, But Differently
slides.subheadline: The drone needs a carried walkthrough; the Rover explores autonomously.

items.title: Ring Drone Cam
items.body: Maps indoor floor plans after customers carry it through the spaces.

items.title: Ring Rover Cam
items.body: Maps indoor floor plans through autonomous exploration.

slides.svgBlueprint: Draw one large schematic indoor floor plan, explicitly illustrative and without dimensions. Overlay two visually distinct mapping traces: a dashed carried walkthrough and a dotted autonomous exploration path. Attach the drone explanation above-left and Rover explanation below-right. Do not imply simultaneous operation, shared maps, or measured coverage.

slides.headline: Eight Minutes, With Conditions Attached
slides.subheadline: Flight duration is conditional; scheduled routes require an Amazon Ring Protect subscription.

items.title: 8 minutes
items.body: Flight limit: new, fully-charged battery under controlled conditions.

items.title: Scheduled Routes
items.body: Set-route and scheduled patrol capability requires an Amazon Ring Protect subscription.

slides.svgBlueprint: Make the numeral 8 the dominant vector element, with minutes set beside it and the full battery-condition statement directly below. End a short flight trace at a simple charging-dock outline. Use a separate bottom rail for the subscription requirement. Avoid countdown ticks, battery percentages, or implied real-world endurance.

slides.headline: Ordinary Surfaces Can Complicate Drone Navigation
slides.subheadline: Amazon identifies three surface categories where navigation performance may degrade.

items.title: Reflective Surfaces
items.body: Examples include polished marble or wet tile.

items.title: Featureless Walls
items.body: Blank matte walls without features may degrade navigation.

items.title: Transparent Surfaces
items.body: Amazon lists frameless glass and mirrors.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use three full-width material bands rather than cards. Illustrate reflection with a doubled ray, a blank wall with an untextured rectangle, and transparent surfaces with offset outlines. Place one concise label and body beside each material illustration. Use interrupted navigation traces to indicate possible degradation, never certain collisions.

slides.headline: Rover Extends Its View Indoors
slides.subheadline: Amazon describes broad coverage, designated scans, and an automatically adjustable mast.

items.title: Claimed Coverage
items.body: Up to 5,000 square feet (465 square meters), according to Amazon.

items.title: Designated Scan
items.body: Can perform a 360-degree scan at a designated location.

items.title: Adjustable Mast
items.body: Automatically adjusts to view over counters, shelving, and other obstacles.

slides.svgBlueprint: Center an abstract wheeled camera with a vertically adjustable mast. Place exactly three annotation zones around it: coverage, scan, and mast. Draw a circular scan arrow and a schematic counter silhouette. Represent coverage with an irregular dotted enclosure, not a measured radius. Do not imply mast height, dimensions, or guaranteed coverage.

slides.headline: Rover Cannot Patrol Every Indoor Floor
slides.subheadline: Stairs, transitions, and incompatible surfaces constrain where it can operate.

items.title: Single Floor
items.body: Indoor operation only; Rover cannot climb stairs.

items.title: Flooring Transitions
items.body: Transitions greater than 1.375 inches (3.5 centimeters) are incompatible.

items.title: Other Incompatibilities
items.body: Curved edges, sunken areas, and black glossy floors are incompatible.

slides.svgBlueprint: Build one continuous architectural floor cross-section divided into three annotation regions. Show a stair interruption, a transition marked with the exact greater-than threshold, and a composite incompatible-surface region. Terminate the Rover path before obstacles. Keep all geometry schematic; do not imply transitions at or below the threshold are universally safe.

slides.headline: Cloud Storage Meets Ring's Security History
slides.subheadline: Current retention terms sit alongside earlier FTC findings about Ring safeguards.

items.label: FTC investigation year
items.body: Ring faced charges over employees and contractors watching customers' private-space recordings.

items.label: US customers' accounts accessed by hackers
items.body: The FTC attributed that access to inadequate Ring safeguards.

items.label: Rover cloud video storage: up to this many days
items.body: Applies to doorbell rings, motion events, and Live View events.

slides.svgBlueprint: Draw three typographic ledger rows with oversized numerical badges. Group the first two under historical Ring context; separate the current Rover storage row with a strong rule and extra whitespace. Use no connecting trend line: these are different measures. Ensure the graphic does not imply the new devices experienced the historical breaches.

slides.headline: Encryption Claims Need A Crucial Distinction
slides.subheadline: The article does not specify encryption-key retention or deletion policies.

items.title: Amazon
items.body: Says both devices' videos receive Ring's Throw Away the Key Encryption.

items.title: Electronic Frontier Foundation
items.body: Says the encryption remains well short of end-to-end encryption.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use a wide editorial column for Amazon's attributed claim and a narrower, accent-lined margin for the EFF's attributed caveat. Connect them with a thin bracket, not an equivalence sign. Place the missing key-policy information prominently beneath the headline. Avoid lock-check icons, key-deletion animations, or diagrams implying verified cryptographic architecture.
